name: Plan reservoir levels and water releases (weekly water plan)
summary: Each week a hydro scheduler turns weather forecasts, snowpack and current reservoir levels into a plan for how much water each of the seventeen hydro plants will release, hour by hour, over the coming week. The plan must keep every water licence limit and, from mid-May to early July, the Ghost Reservoir elevation the province sets for flood protection, while placing as much generation as possible in the highest-price hours that the trading desk expects. The scheduler, the desk's portfolio optimisation analyst, a hydro area manager and the control centre all touch the plan. It is slow and error-prone because inflow forecasts are uncertain in spring, constraints are kept in spreadsheets, and the plan is re-keyed into the desk's offer tools and revised mid-week when weather changes.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with seventeen hydro plants on the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman rivers run from one Calgary control centre, alongside converted gas units and wind farms.
baseline.notes: Planning was done in spreadsheets and in-house models fed by a historian, with email as the hand-off. Only weekly planning is in this file; daily dispatch is in the operate-plants workflow and flood events in the flood operations process.

trigger: The weekly planning cycle starts when new weather forecasts arrive midweek for the following operating week.
end_state: The approved plan has been run for its week, any mid-week revisions have been issued, and planned versus actual results are recorded.

volume.seasonality: One plan a week all year. Mid-week revisions are more frequent from May to July during snowmelt and June rain, and the Ghost coordination with the province happens only from May 16 to July 7.

evidence.note: Weekly cadence from the process map; 52 plans a year is 4.3 a month.

surge.cause: spring snowmelt and June rain (plan revised two or three times a week)

evidence.note: Flood-control window May 16 to July 7 (s3); revision frequency during runoff is an estimate.

TransAlta's control centre operators coordinate with a Hydro Scheduling function (s5); the organisation file has no hydro scheduling role. Cost and FTE are tier C estimates set like a plant engineer (75 to 115 CAD/h loaded, wage x 1.40).
Share of a desk analyst's week spent on the hydro plan; estimate.
About half an hour a week of review across three area managers; estimate.
Plan reading at shift start; estimate.

systems.name: Load, price, wind and inflow forecasting models
Document management and engineering drawings repository
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Energy trading and risk management system
Hydro, wind and battery SCADA and remote control

steps.name: Gather weather and snowpack data
steps.description: The hydro scheduler opens the weather providers' seven- to ten-day forecasts of precipitation and freezing levels for the Bow, North Saskatchewan and Oldman headwaters, the latest provincial water supply outlook and the snow pillow readings, and saves them to the weekly planning folder.

error.defect_description: A stale or wrong-basin forecast is downloaded.

evidence.note: The outlook is issued monthly January to August and snow pillow data come from 18 sites (s7). The planning cycle start and the time taken are estimates.

steps.name: Pull last week's levels and flows
steps.description: A scheduled historian report exports last week's hourly reservoir elevations, plant flows, spill and gauge flows into the planning workbook so the scheduler starts from actual storage, without anyone keying the numbers.

error.defect_description: A gauge or tag drops out and leaves a gap in the export.

evidence.note: Standard historian-to-spreadsheet export assumed for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Update inflow forecast by basin
steps.description: The scheduler runs the inflow models for each storage system (Spray and Kananaskis lakes, Ghost and Bearspaw on the Bow, Bighorn and Brazeau on the North Saskatchewan, and the small Oldman plants), feeding in the weather, snowpack and observed flows, and produces daily inflow volumes for the next one to four weeks.

error.defect_description: The forecast misses a rain-on-snow event or the timing of melt.

evidence.note: Reservoir systems and plants from s6; forecast inputs from s7. Model run time is an estimate.

steps.name: Check forecast against observed inflow
steps.description: The scheduler compares the model's back-cast for the last seven days with the observed inflows calculated from storage change and outflow. Where they diverge by more than about ten percent the scheduler adjusts snowmelt or loss parameters and re-runs the model.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: forecast does not track; model re-run

evidence.note: Back-casting check and rerun rate are estimates of common practice.

steps.name: Compile licence and agreement constraints
steps.description: The scheduler lists the week's limits in the workbook: water licence minimum flows and reservoir elevation ranges, ramping limits, deliveries owed to irrigation districts and municipalities, and from May 16 to July 7 the Ghost Reservoir target elevation set by the province, plus the Kananaskis drought volume target.

error.defect_description: An elevation limit or minimum flow is entered wrongly.

control.basis: Water Act licence conditions and the Alberta-TransAlta Bow River agreement (Ghost flood-season targets, Kananaskis drought targets)

evidence.note: Ghost window May 16 to July 7 and Kananaskis volume targets (s3); deliveries to irrigation districts and municipalities (s4).

steps.name: Collect planned unit outages and capability
steps.description: The scheduler checks the outage schedule in the ERP and the control centre's equipment status log for units that will be out or derated during the week, and emails the hydro supervisors to confirm dates that are still moving.

error.defect_description: A late outage change is not captured.

evidence.note: Estimate; outage dates often move with crew availability.

steps.name: Provide hourly price and market view
steps.description: The portfolio optimisation analyst sends the expected hourly price shape for the coming week, the ancillary services the desk plans to sell from hydro and the hedged positions the hydro output should cover, so the water can be placed in the highest-value hours.

error.defect_description: The price shape is out of date after a market event.

evidence.note: Hydro is sold merchant in the spot market and earns capacity, energy and ancillary services value (s6). Time is an estimate.

steps.name: Run weekly release optimisation
steps.description: The scheduler runs the weekly optimisation workbook or model, which spreads each reservoir's usable water over the week's hours so that more is generated in the expected high-price hours while keeping all limits, and produces hourly release and MW ranges by plant group with end-of-week reservoir levels.

error.defect_description: A constraint or volume is set up wrongly in the model.

evidence.note: Optimisation by spreadsheet or in-house model assumed for 2019-2022; time estimated.

steps.name: Check schedule against limits
steps.description: The scheduler checks every reservoir trajectory and river flow in the draft against the constraint table, looks for hours that break a minimum flow or ramp limit, and decides whether the result is feasible and sensible or needs another run.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Water Act licence conditions: minimum flows and elevation limits

next.condition: flood-control window May 16 to July 7: Ghost plan goes to the province
limit broken or result implausible; re-run

evidence.note: Share of weeks in the May 16 to July 7 window from s3 (about 7.5 of 52 weeks); rerun rate estimated.

steps.name: Send Ghost elevation plan to the province
steps.description: During the flood-control window the scheduler emails the planned Ghost Reservoir elevations and outflows to the provincial river forecasters and water managers, with the inflow forecast behind them, and asks them to confirm or change the target elevation.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Alberta-TransAlta Bow River agreement: province may set Ghost target elevations May 16 to July 7

evidence.note: Target-setting right and window from s3.

steps.name: Province confirms or changes Ghost target
steps.description: Provincial forecasters review the plan against their own flood forecast for Calgary and reply with the target elevation for the coming days, which may be lower than planned when heavy rain is forecast.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Province sets targets and both parties assess elevations (s3); reply time and change rate estimated.

steps.name: Draft weekly water plan
steps.description: The scheduler writes the weekly water plan: daily energy and volume by plant group, hourly MW ranges, planned spill, reservoir trajectories with limits, and notes on inflow risk and outages, in the standard workbook and a one-page summary.

error.defect_description: Summary figures do not match the workbook.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Desk reviews plan
steps.description: The portfolio optimisation analyst checks that the plan's hourly energy fits the offer strategy, the ancillary services commitments and the hedges, and either accepts it or asks for water to be moved between days or plant groups.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Area manager reviews and approves plan
steps.description: The hydro area manager checks the plan for site issues the model does not see, such as crews working below a dam, public events on a river, ice conditions or a landowner complaint, and approves the plan or sends it back with changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Hydro operating procedures: weekly plan approved by the accountable area manager

evidence.note: Public safety concerns below dams (water can rise 2 m quickly near Bearspaw) from s4; approval step and times estimated.

steps.name: Publish plan to desk and control centre
steps.description: The scheduler saves the approved plan to the shared folder and emails it to the real-time desk, the portfolio optimisation team and the hydro control centre, with a short note on what changed from last week.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Key plan into offer and forecast tools
steps.description: The portfolio optimisation analyst re-keys the daily energy limits and hourly MW ranges by plant group into the generation forecast and offer-building spreadsheets used by the real-time traders.
outputs: hydro energy limits in offer tools

error.defect_description: Volume keyed into the wrong hour block or plant group.

evidence.note: Re-keying between the plan workbook and desk tools assumed for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Control centre turns plan into daily guidelines
steps.description: A hydro control centre operator reads the plan at the start of shift, checks it against current equipment status and gate settings, and asks the scheduler about anything that cannot be run, such as a unit already out or a gate restricted.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Operators coordinate with Hydro Scheduling and work 12-hour shifts (s5); times estimated.

steps.name: Track plan against actual each day
steps.description: Each weekday morning the scheduler compares actual inflow, generation and reservoir levels with the plan and the latest weather, and decides whether the deviation is large enough to revise the rest of the week. The minutes shown are the total for the week.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: inflow or price deviates enough to revise

evidence.note: Revision rate estimated; higher during spring runoff.

steps.name: Issue mid-week revision
steps.description: The scheduler re-runs the optimisation for the remaining days with the new inflow or price view, checks limits, and emails revised daily volumes to the desk and control centre, phoning the real-time desk lead if the change affects offers already submitted.

error.defect_description: Revision sent to the desk but not to the control centre, or the reverse.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Review week and archive
steps.description: At the end of the planning week the scheduler records planned versus actual generation, spill and end-of-week levels by reservoir, notes forecast errors and their causes, and files the plan for the licence reporting and for next season's calibration.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Province changes the Ghost target
exceptions.description: During the flood-control window the province lowers the Ghost target because heavy rain is forecast, and the week is re-optimised around less storage.

exceptions.name: Mid-week revision
exceptions.description: Inflow or prices move enough that the rest of the week is re-planned and re-sent.

exceptions.name: Forecast does not track observed inflow
exceptions.description: The back-cast misses last week's inflow and the inflow model is recalibrated before planning.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from start of preparation to end-of-week review
benchmarks.population: Weekly hydro plans at a multi-reservoir merchant hydro fleet

evidence.note: About two days of preparation before the operating week plus the seven-day week and a day to close it out; no published benchmark found.

benchmarks.unit: days a year (May 16 to July 7) when the province may set Ghost target elevations

pain_points.description: Inflow forecasts are least reliable in exactly the weeks when the plan matters most (snowmelt and June rain), so plans are revised mid-week and offers restated.

evidence.note: Estimate from the structure of the task.

pain_points.description: Licence limits, agreement targets and outage dates are kept in spreadsheets and copied by hand into the model, and a wrong limit is caught only at the check step or not at all.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: The approved plan is re-keyed into the desk's offer and forecast tools, a second copy that can drift from the plan.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Bow River Basin: TransAlta operations
sources.supports: Agreement since May 2016 (extended to April 1, 2031): from May 16 to July 7 the province may set target elevations for Ghost Reservoir (up to 65 million m3 for flood mitigation) and year-round volume targets for the Kananaskis-area reservoirs (up to 40 million m3 for drought mitigation); TransAlta decides how to meet the targets; the province and TransAlta assess elevations together each year; compensation 5.5 million CAD per year.

sources.title: Hydro safety
sources.supports: Water levels near Bearspaw Dam can rise or fall up to 2 metres in a short time; hydro operations support flood control, drought mitigation and irrigation and convey water to licence holders including irrigation districts and municipalities; buffer zones, signs, booms and barriers; regular patrols, inspections, safety audits and infrastructure maintenance; coordination with regulators, police and emergency responders.

sources.title: Hydro Generation Operator I (Calgary) job posting
sources.supports: Operators in the Calgary Hydro System Control Centre remotely monitor and operate the hydro fleet through SCADA on rotating 12-hour day and night shifts; execute AESO dispatches, ancillary services directives and voltage instructions and monitor AGC; manage reservoirs, forebays, canals and river flows within operating constraints; acknowledge and respond to alarms; coordinate switching, isolations, equipment status and after-hours response with site operations, maintenance and Hydro Scheduling; keep electronic operating logs and shift handovers. Posted November 2026, after the reference period.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Alberta hydro facilities: Bow River system 11 plants (338 MW: Barrier, Bearspaw, Cascade, Ghost, Horseshoe, Interlakes, Kananaskis, Pocaterra, Rundle, Spray, Three Sisters), North Saskatchewan system 2 plants (Bighorn 120 MW, Brazeau 355 MW), Oldman system 4 small plants (21 MW); merchant sale into the Alberta spot market after PPA expiry; value from capacity, energy and ancillary services; Belly River operates April to October.

sources.title: Drought: current conditions (water supply outlook, snowpack and reservoir storage)
sources.supports: Water supply outlook published in the second week of each month from January to August, estimating runoff volume at 20 locations; mountain snow surveys monthly February 1 to June 1 and automated snow pillow data at 18 sites; storage in major irrigation and hydroelectric reservoirs updated each weekday in the Provincial Reservoir Storage Summary.

assumptions: The organisation file lists no hydro scheduling role, although TransAlta's control centre coordinates with a Hydro Scheduling function (s5). A hydro scheduler is added with not_in_org_file; in the organisation file the portfolio optimisation analyst would otherwise have to do this work.
The planning week starts with data gathering midweek and the plan runs Saturday to Friday; cycle time includes the operating week, so most of it is calendar time, not work.
Loaded costs follow the organisation file (wage x 1.40). The hydro scheduler is costed like a plant engineer.
Flood events themselves are handled in hyd-flood-operations; this file covers only ordinary weekly planning, including the routine Ghost target exchange with the province.
Hands-on time is about 23 hours a plan (median), mostly the scheduler; the remaining scheduler time goes to daily scheduling and reporting not modelled here.
